evals.name: hello-world-no-database
evals.source: Synthetic user scenario. Real Next.js app and PostgreSQL; simulated v0 integration tool. No database exists or is connected until the agent requests one. Not a live v0 or Marketplace test.
evals.prompt: Add prisma database to my hello world app
evals.expected_output: The existing Hello World app gains a database through the host integration flow, defaults to Prisma ORM 8, and passes independent application and database-readiness checks.
expectations: Obtains and connects one database through the supplied GetOrRequestIntegration tool, rather than a separate cloud provisioning path; does not claim a real Vercel installation.
Defaults to Prisma ORM 8, loads prisma-orm-setup and the matching package-owned prisma-8 guidance, and uses that ORM from server-side application code.
Uses the injected connection, preserves the unrelated HELLO_GREETING setting and Hello World page, and keeps connection values out of client code and the final response.
The independent verifier confirms the app builds and type-checks, serves Hello World, and has a working readiness endpoint that fails when its database is unavailable and recovers afterward.

host.context: You are editing project/, a Hello World Next.js app in a simulated v0 host. The selected workspace is hello-workspace, project hello-world, region local. No database exists or is connected, and DATABASE_URL is absent. The host provides GetOrRequestIntegration to inspect or request its integration; the host performs local provisioning and environment injection. Read the app's existing README and configuration. Only this host tool may acquire a database. All database operations stay local; do not call cloud provisioning services. The simulation has already authorized connecting a disposable database.
